title: Tlatelolco
summary: Tlatelolco was the Mexica twin city of Tenochtitlan on the island lake, founded around 1338 by a group that split from the Tenochca. Its great market served both islands and the Triple Alliance. After defeat by Axayacatl of Tenochtitlan in 1473 it came under its rival's control.

uncertainty.note: Founding date follows chronicles cited by INAH. The end marks loss of independence; the city continued under Tenochtitlan until the Spanish conquest.

as_recorded.value: independent until 1473; conquest under Axayacatl (year 7 casa, 1473)

where.modern_name: Tlatelolco, Cuauhtemoc borough, Mexico City, Mexico
where.historical_name: Tlatelolco, Mexica altepetl on the island of Lake Texcoco, twin of Mexico-Tenochtitlan

importance.justification: A major Mexica city whose market was the commercial hub of the island capitals and the Triple Alliance.

sources.title: Zona arqueologica de Tlatelolco
sources.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Antropologia e Historia (Mexico)

sources.title: El mercado de Tlatelolco (Alejandra Davila Montoya)

reviewer_note: Dates are from chronicles; INAH and UNAM agree on 1473. The 1968 massacre is a separate stub (1968-10-02-tlatelolco-massacre) and was not researched here. The 1521 end of Mexica rule was not on the opened pages.

beats.caption: Mexica chronicles place the founding of Tlatelolco after a group split from the Tenochca of Tenochtitlan.
Its great market was a trading hub for both islands and the Triple Alliance.
Tlatelolco lost independence after fighting Tenochtitlan; control of the market passed to the victors, who held it when the Spanish arrived.
